tools.name: fs_read

Binary documents use the shared bounded ingestion readers and return extraction metadata. If the format or reader is unavailable, the result is terminal and names the missing capability; do not retry with another tool. Use offset and limit for large text.

tools.name: fs_grep
tools.description: Search the project workspace for a regular expression. In Full access, an explicit absolute host path is also allowed. For user-file discovery outside the workspace, use the current user's home, /mnt, or /media; do not use / unless the user explicitly requests an entire system search with entire_system=true. Protected virtual/system trees are skipped and reported. Each search inspects at most 10,000 filesystem entries and returns scanned_entries and search_truncated; do not repeat a partial search. Use output_mode 'files_with_matches' to list matching files, 'count' for per-file counts, or 'content' for the matching lines.

glob.description: Only search files whose name matches this pattern, such as '*.py'.

max_results.description: Largest number of results to return.

tools.name: fs_glob
tools.description: List project workspace paths by name pattern, such as '**/*.ts' or '*.md'. In Full access, an explicit absolute host path is also allowed. For user-file discovery outside the workspace, use the current user's home, /mnt, or /media; do not use / unless the user explicitly requests an entire system search with entire_system=true. For one exact filename in Full access, omit path: the tool searches the workspace and current user's home, then /mnt and /media as budget permits, stopping at the first match. Every search inspects at most 10,000 filesystem entries and returns scanned_entries and search_truncated; do not repeat a search when it reports truncation. Protected virtual/system trees are skipped and reported. Use it to discover the files a task touches.

tools.name: workflow_run
tools.description:
Run a workflow that fans work out across many child agents and return the workflow's final value. Use this when the user asks for a workflow, or for work that splits across many independent pieces: an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, or an adversarial check of findings. For one or two delegations, call the subagent tool directly instead.

Two forms are accepted:
- 'name': the name of a workflow document installed under .averqel/workflows in the project workspace. The document lists the steps and the dependencies between them; each step runs as its own agent.
- 'script': a JavaScript orchestration script. Its hooks are:
  * workflow.agent(task, options?) - run one child agent to completion and resolve to its answer. options: {label, phase, mode, persona, model, provider, tool_allow, tool_deny, schema}. With no schema the answer is the child's text. With a schema the answer is the validated JSON object, or null when the child failed or did not match the schema. A schema is an object-rooted JSON Schema using only type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf.
  * workflow.parallel(items, mapper, options?) - run mapper over every item and resolve to the results in order. options: {concurrency}.
  * workflow.pipeline(items, ...stages) - run every item through the stages; each stage receives (previous, item, index) and the hook resolves to one result per item. A stage that throws drops that item to null and skips its remaining stages. workflow.pipeline(stages, {initial}) is also accepted and runs one value through the stages in order.
  * workflow.phase(title) - start a progress phase. workflow.log(message) - narrate progress. workflow.args - this call's input, verbatim.
  * End the script with 'return <value>'; that value is the tool's result.
  * Misused hooks (a bad argument, an unknown option, an unsupported schema, a tripped agent cap) end the whole script instead of producing null. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

function.description:
Run a workflow that fans work out across many child agents and return the workflow's final value. Use this when the user asks for a workflow, or for work that splits across many independent pieces: an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, or an adversarial check of findings. For one or two delegations, call the subagent tool directly instead.

Two forms are accepted:
- 'name': the name of a workflow document installed under .averqel/workflows in the project workspace. The document lists the steps and the dependencies between them; each step runs as its own agent.
- 'script': a JavaScript orchestration script. Its hooks are:
  * workflow.agent(task, options?) - run one child agent to completion and resolve to its answer. options: {label, phase, mode, persona, model, provider, tool_allow, tool_deny, schema}. With no schema the answer is the child's text. With a schema the answer is the validated JSON object, or null when the child failed or did not match the schema. A schema is an object-rooted JSON Schema using only type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf.
  * workflow.parallel(items, mapper, options?) - run mapper over every item and resolve to the results in order. options: {concurrency}.
  * workflow.pipeline(items, ...stages) - run every item through the stages; each stage receives (previous, item, index) and the hook resolves to one result per item. A stage that throws drops that item to null and skips its remaining stages. workflow.pipeline(stages, {initial}) is also accepted and runs one value through the stages in order.
  * workflow.phase(title) - start a progress phase. workflow.log(message) - narrate progress. workflow.args - this call's input, verbatim.
  * End the script with 'return <value>'; that value is the tool's result.

tools.name: run_code

The program receives a 'tool' function: call tool('web_search', {'query': '...'}) and it returns that tool's result. The program runs in a confined sandbox with no network, so every piece of data it needs must come from a tool call. Print what you want to see and return a value to hand it back. Use this for a loop over many items or a multi-step calculation that would otherwise need one provider round trip per step. Supports Python and JavaScript (Node.js) languages.
